Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

By way of present judgment/award, I shall dispose of the DAR filed by the investigating agency which has been converted into a claim petition under section 166(4) of M. V. Act 1988 for grant of compensation to the petitioner.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 08.04.2017, the petitioner/injured was posted as ASI Traffic Circle Narela, Delhi and was performing his duty at Alipur Road, Holambi Khurd Road, Near Midda Farm Crossing.

At about 11:45 AM, offending vehicle (canter) bearing registration no. PB-10CF-1305 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS.
Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 manner, came from Alipur side and hit against one Eeco Car bearing registration no. DL1LW-3214 with a great force and due to said forceful impact, the said Eeco Car came towards the petitioner and hit him badly.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi where he was medically examined vide MLC bearing No. 1905 dated 08.04.2017.
A case U/s 279/337 IPC was registered at P.S. Narela vide FIR No. 278/17 with regard to the accident in question.

The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 3, insured with respondent no. 4/National Insurance Co. Ltd and was in possession of respondent no. 2 as on the date of accident in question.

3. The respondent no.1, 2 & 3 i.e. driver, possessory owner and registered owner have failed to file their WS despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities and consequently, their defence was struck off vide order dated 12.10.2017.
4.

In its WS, the respondent no.4 i.e. insurance company has not taken any statutory defence, as available U/s 149(2) MV Act, to exonerate its legal liability qua the insured vehicle i.e. the offending vehicle (canter) bearing registration no.PB-10CF-1305.

However, on merits, it is claimed that as per DAR and annexed site plan, the other vehicle i.e. Eeco car bearing registration no. DL1LW-3214 was being driven in utter violation of traffic rules, which caused the accident in question, thereby,
injuring the claimant who was on police duty at the accident spot, thereby, seeking to be absolved MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 from any liability to pay compensation to the petitioner/injured.
It is admitted that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 4, at the time of accident.

From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 12.10.2017:-
1.

Whether the injured Ram Niwas suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 08.04.2017 at 10:45 am, Alipur-Narela Road, Holambi Khurd Road Crossing, Near Minda Farm House, Narela, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS. Narela due to rashness and negligence on the part of Arvind who was driving Truck bearing registration no. PB10-CF-1305, possessed by Sh. Parveen Chaudhary/R2, owned by Sh. Kuldeep Singh/R3 and insured with National Insurance Co Ltd?
OPP 2.
Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

7. In defence, no evidence has been adduced by any of the respondents and their opportunity to lead respondent's evidence was closed vide order dated 21.12.2022.
MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 8.

Record shows that interest of petitioner was closed as he has failed to conclude his evidence.

petitioner/injured examined himself as PW1 by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A).
In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A), injured/petitioner has deposed on the lines of averments made in the DAR petition.

He deposed that at about 11:45 AM, offending vehicle (canter) bearing registration no. PB-10CF-1305 which was being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein) in a very high rash and negligent manner, came from Alipur side and hit against one Eeco Car bearing registration no. 12.

The aforesaid witness (PW1) was duly cross examined by the Ld. Counsel for the insurance company on the aspect of under consideration where he deposed that he became unconscious immediately after the MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 accident.
He deposed that the FIR in the matter was not registered on his statement.
He deposed that two vehicles were involved in the accident.
He admitted that he was hit by Eeco Car.
Counsel for the petitioner argued that the accident in question has taken place due to sole negligence of the driver of the offending canter bearing registration no. PB-10F-1305.

He further argued that if the said offending canter would have not in high speed, the accident in question could have been averted, as the same was in such a high speed that the driver of the offending canter could not control it and consequently hit the eeco car from right rear side of the car, which has resulted that eeco car hit the petitioner who was on his duty at the spot of accident and inspecting the vehicles being posted in Delhi Traffic Police.

16. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that insurance company could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination.

Said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross- examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
Furthermore, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 278/17 u/s 279/337 IPC
was registered at PS. Narela with regard to accident in question
. Copy of said FIR (which is part of DAR), would show that same was registered on the statement of Ct. Lokesh on the date of accident itself.
The contents of said FIR would show that complainant Ct. Lokesh had disclosed the same sequence of facts leading to the accident, as deposed by PW1 during the course of inquiry.
The registration number of offending vehicle to be PB10-CF-1305 is also disclosed therein.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.

17. Respondent no. 1 was charge-sheeted(which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/338 IPC would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver (respondent no.1 herein) and same also points out towards the fact that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

Perusal of the mechanical inspection report dated 08.04.2017 (which is the part of DAR Ex. PW1/6)
of the offending vehicle would show fresh damages i.e. its front side MACP No. 645/17; FIR No.
287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 bumper scratched & damaged and front side extra fitted foot board damaged.

Likewise, copy of mechanical inspection report dated 08.04.2017 (which also part of DAR Ex. PW1/6) of ECCO car which has hit the injured/petitioner would show that its right side body & door damaged, right side tail light damaged, left side body scratched & dented, left rear side wheel rim slightly bended & wheel tyre dislocated and body frame bended.

The mechanical inspection reports of both the vehicles corraborates the mannerism of ocurance of the accident as deposed by the petitioner himself as PW1, which resulted grievous injuries upon the petitioner.

Further the site plan filed by the IO shows that the alleged offending vehicle (canter) hit the EECO car at point 'A', the alleged offending vehicle (canter) after the accident found at point 'B', the EECO car after the accident was found at point 'C' and the injured/petitioner ASI Ram Avtar was standing at point 'D' where the EECO car hit him, supporting the case of the claimant that he sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

18. It is not disputed that respondent no.,3 is the registered owner of the offending canter in question, which was being driven by respondent no.1, at the instance of respondent no. 2 as its possessory owner. Respondent no.1 was arrested in the criminal case pertaining to the road accident in question.

He himself through his own testimony or any other witness or evidence in any manner,
failed to throw light upon circumstances, under which the accident in question has taken place.

19. Perusal of medical records, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of injured prepared at SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi shows that he was removed to said hospital on 08.04.2017 at about 12:20 pm with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.

The said injuries have been opined as 'grievous' and it has been proved on record by way of medical certificate Ex.PW1/1 and corresponding medical bills tendered as Ex.PW1/2 that the claimant was constrained to remain off duty for about two months.

The nature of injuries, medical treatment record and the time period of treatment, are consistent to prove that the injured Ram Niwas suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident on 08.04.2017, as per the case of the claimant.

20. In view of the aforesaid discussion, it is established in accordance with law that the petitioner Ram Niwas has sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 08.04.2017 at about 11:45 am at Alipur-Narela Road, Holambi Khurd Road Crossing, near Minda Farm House,
Narela, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 21.

Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

22. The Hon'ble Apex Court pleased to consider the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation and has laid down the binding guidelines that " the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

sentences.text:
The golden principles for assessment of adequate compensation to victims of road accident have been appreciated by the full bench of Hon'ble Apex Court in 2017 (13) SCALE 12 : 2017 XI AD (SC) 113 titled National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., wherein it has been held:-
"

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: .....The Tribunal and the Courts have to bear in mind that the basic principle lies in pragmatic computation which is in proximity to reality.
It is a well expected norm that money can not substitute a life lost but an effort has to be made for grant of just compensation having uniformity of approach.
There has to be a balance between the two extremes, that is, a windfall and the pittance, a bonanza and the modicum....."

23. In view of the findings on issue no.1 hereinabove, it is established that the injured/petitioner Ram Niwas sustained grievous injury in the road traffic accident occurred on 08.04.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1/driver.

Consequent upon the injuries, the MACP No.
645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 injured/petitioner suffered both physical and Asi Ram Niwas vs Arvind on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135807208/
6 internal injuries, pain & suffering, incurred medical expenses, remained incapacitated to resume work immediately and therefore, suffered both personally and monetarily.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

24. Firstly, quantum of medical expenses, has been proved by the petitioner by way of evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/1) that after the accident, he was taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi and thereafter, he was referred to Max Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi.
He claimed that he has spent Rs. 35,480/- on his treatment.

He has relied upon medical bills Ex. PW1/2(colly) & Ex.
PW1/5(colly).
During his cross-
examination on behalf of insurance company
, he admitted that his medical treatment and all the expenses were covered by his office.
He further denied the suggestion that all his medical bills were reimbursed by his department and that is why, he has not filed the originals thereof on record.
The petitioner/injured is a regular employee of Delhi Police.
He has failed to substantiate the amount of medical bills which have not been reimbursed by his office.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

25. It is further claimed that petitioner has spent considerable amount on his special diet,
conveyance and attendant.

It is relevant to note here that the petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence to prove the amount, if any spent on special diet, conveyance and attendant as aforesaid MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 by him.
There is nothing from medical record to show that any attendant was needed during the treatment period of the petitioner.
The injuries sustained by the victim were primarily multiple abrasion on left hand/occipital region and on right shoulder.
Subsequently, the radiologist has opined fracture of 2 nd / 3rd /4th rib thereby suggesting the injuries to be grievous in nature.
In these facts and circumstances, grant of a composite sum of Rs. 25,000/- towards ancillary medical expenses, conveyance charges and special diet to the petitioner is reasonable.
26. The petitioner shall also be entitled to any loss on account of earnings, if any, owing to the grievous injuries sustained by him in the road accident in question.
It is matter of record that injured namely Sh. Ram Niwas (PW1) was posted as ASI in Delhi Police at the time of accident in question.

PW1 has proved vide medical certificate collectively tendered as Ex.PW1/1 that he remained on bed rest/off duty for a period of 59 days and requisite medical leaves in this regard were debited from his leave account.
It is also brought forth that the petitioner did not suffer any loss of pay for the aforesaid 59 days.
The petitioner has filed on record his salary slip for the Month of November, 2016 and his identity card which are the part of DAR Ex. PW1/6.
As per the said pay slip, the petitioner was drawing a basic pay to the tune of Rs. 46,200/- per month and DA to the tune of Rs. 924/- per month.
The petitioner suffered deduction of about two months medical leave from his service leave account which he could have availed, as per his needs.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for loss of entitled MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS.
Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 leave due to the injuries sustained in the accident in question.

For the purpose of calculating the leaves and the encashment of commuted leaves is based what was the salary drawn by the person under Rule 40 of CCS (Leaves) Rules which includes basic pay +
Dearness Allowance.

At the time of accident, the basic pay of the petitioner Ram Niwas was Rs.
46,200/- and dearness allowance was Rs. 924/-, thereby, comes to Rs. 47,124/- per month.

Thus,
the compensation on account of loss of income, being granted in lieu of loss of leave entitlement,

7 would be computed as half pay commuted leave for a period of two months.

MACP No. 645/17; FIR No. 287/17; PS. Narela DOD: 19.08.2023 (ii) The medical records and treatment taken by the petitioner duly proved as Ex.PW1/2 reveals that the petitioner underwent treatment for about 4 months, though, he remained off duty for about two months.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries, period of treatment and inconvenience suffered by the petitioner, it is considered reasonable to award a sum of Rs. 50,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
28. Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Insurance company did not adduce any evidence as it had no statutory defence.
It is nowhere the case of insurance company that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/violated by insured.

Keeping in view the existence of valid insurance policy and in the absence of any statutory defences available to the insurance company, insurance company concerned is legally liable to pay the compensation amount.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.
